contract.blank: workflow_incomplete; mapped for audit but never silently scored
contract.UNC: canonical unclear and numeric contribution 0 plus uncertainty flag
contract.NA: excluded only from the relevant subindicator denominator
contract.multi_report: one study weight; union complementary evidence; preserve contradictions

none.rule: no explicit metric-level or textual comparator

internal.rule: matched comparator/baseline internal to the study

external_or_common.rule: explicit external, public, conventional, standard, prior-work, or benchmark comparator

workflow_blank_audit.rule: These are mapped to workflow_blank for unmapped QA, but must be resolved, declared not-applicable, or excluded as non-outcome/configuration rows before final scoring.

baseline.raw: ACO-OFDM-4QAM-LFM is compared with 4QAM-LFM under three turbulence levels. The integrated waveform is reported to improve BER by 4.2 dB and to have a more peg-like ambiguity function with better range and velocity resolution.

PCS-16/32/64-QAM is compared across distance with FFE and a 10-tap second-order VNLE; the burst's SNR-predicted GMI is checked against measured per-subcarrier GMI. Complexity is contrasted with neural-network and transformer ranging. No separate sensing waveform/hardware or matched independent-radar baseline is tested.

BPF, MLP and AMLP phase extraction are compared; generated and experimental background noise are compared using PCA/CDF; BER with and without 30-kHz vibration is compared. The 2025 conference version supplies an earlier ANN-only 12-dB result.

Communication BER/MSE and ranging RMSE compare EADO-OFDM against DCO-OFDM and ADO-OFDM, with 16-QAM/BPSK variants; sensing processing compares element-wise division against cross-correlation and optical against electrical power detection.
Single SOP/single FrFT versus dual SOP/dual FrFT; conventional CMA-AEQ versus FFD-AEQ; QPSK versus 16-QAM; SCPR sweep; companion conference report provides shorter report-specific metrics.

Communication without FD-NOMA and FD-NOMA with or without SIC; polarization sensing from conventional MIMO equalizer Stokes parameters; SCPR and OSNR sweeps. Cross-paper benchmark values are declared non-unified because conditions differ.

Communication SNR is compared across launch powers and BER/SNR across distance. HLLB circulator/FBG routing is contrasted qualitatively with conventional 90/10-coupler HLLB loss. Rayleigh traces are compared with 0, 3, 5 and 10 dB inserted attenuation.

Both reports compare operating conditions within the same chip (mirror speed, transmitter bias/current and transmitter-only versus on-chip transceiver VLC). They do not test a matched separate-sensor/separate-communication baseline or report BER-based communication comparisons.

The proposed directionless and directional O-ISAC configurations are compared with a separate communication-and-sensing system that assigns half the power to each function. Additional within-study comparisons include uniformity-based versus threshold-based source layout, single versus four-PD reception, and with versus without optimized source distribution/beamforming.

Journal communication baselines are ISFA and conventional FD-VNLE; sensing baselines are FFT and CZT. The conference precursor compares uncompensated, phase-noise-compensated and compensated-plus-CZT radar processing, and communication with versus without BPS.

Communication compares 16-QAM/10-GBaud and 32-QAM/8-GBaud at equal 120-Gbit/s gross rate and four DSP chains. Sensing compares traditional single-channel matched filtering (15-mm theoretical resolution) with three-channel AR coherent fusion (2.5-mm theoretical; 2.3-mm measured for 3-mm spacing), plus ideal versus AR phase-noise simulations.
OCDM and conventional OFDM use identical frames/hardware and are compared for PAPR, BER, SNR distribution, constellation/equalization, range mainlobe, PSLR and ISLR; precoded variants are simulated.

ODDM and OTFS are compared at matched DD-domain parameters in static and partially simulated mobile channels. ODDM improves input-optical-power sensitivity by 1.33 dB and 1.06 dB, respectively, at the 3.8x10^-3 HD-FEC threshold, while both waveforms show the same reported single-target ranging positions and 1-cm maximum error.

Journal simulations compare per-emitter-power, total-power and LP formulations, optimized versus SDR-retrieved solutions, light-field SINR thresholds from 10 to 30 dB, and BER/RMSE across electrical SNR. The conference precursor compares SDR and LP at 15/20/25-dB communication SINR thresholds. No hardware or matched separate-system baseline is tested.

The primary report compares 16-QAM and 64-QAM communication within the same four-sensing/60-communication subcarrier partition and compares conventional division-based with simplified ZF hardware. The conference and companion reports document earlier/parallel 200-m and 100-m versions. There is no sensing-versus-communication subcarrier-allocation sweep, Pareto analysis or independent radar baseline.
The integrated LFM system is compared with conventional single-carrier SHCD across three chirp periods; carrier-phase recovery variants and OFDR phase compensation are also compared.

Communication compares pulse-free baseline, WDM-only LO/pulse co-propagation, polarization-multiplexed co-propagation, and a reduced sensing-pulse-power condition. Sensing compares four-comb-line dual-pulse probing with a single-wavelength Koheras X15 dual-pulse setup at equal power per wavelength.

SF-LFM-OFDM is compared with conventional OFDM for PAPR, BER, SNR and data rate; radar-only SF-LFM is compared with the integrated waveform for cross-correlation amplitude; multiple pulse counts and power ratios are evaluated.
Binary PCE-10:BTPSV-4F and PCE-10:BTPSV-4Cl OPDs; published NIR OPDs for cutoff-frequency context; commercial smartwatch for HR/RR consistency.
Simulated strip-waveguide sensitivity 97 nm/RIU and slot-waveguide sensitivity 197 nm/RIU; silicon thermo-optic sensitivity around 90 pm/degC is cited against 16.2 pm/degC for silicon nitride.
Theoretical 16-QAM AWGN BER trend and the reported pre-FEC BER threshold of 10^-3; literature comparison is descriptive.

Primary experimental comparator is an NKT X15 ultra-narrow-linewidth laser below 100 Hz without LPN compensation. Table 2 also reports secondary literature comparators; those values were not independently source-verified.
Table 1 contrasts the proposed optical framework with RF-ISAC and reports approximate gains without a reproducible common scenario.
DCO-OFDM versus ACO-OFDM; point-source versus area-source channel models.
Natural, sequency and Walsh-Paley Hadamard orderings across sampling ratios; back-to-back communication versus target-plane transmission; sequential TDM versus proposed FDM operation.
Communication-only IM/DD; sensing without communication; earlier common-bias DSCM (CB-DSCM) architecture; MZM-bias and CSPR sweeps.
Sensing with versus without modulated covert communication; covert/public BER with versus without vibration/ASE conditions.
Table 1 compares prior discrete-module and OPA ISAC schemes using FDM, TDM, CTCF and discrete operation; the proposed PAPA row reports 23-us steering, 20-Gbps data rate and 3-cm ranging resolution.
Back-to-back communication is compared with after-transmission communication; probe intervals k=1,2,4,5 are compared for sensing resolution/noise floor.
CC-OTDR off, conventional unshaped CC-OTDR on, and shaped CC-OTDR on are compared for QPSK and 16-QAM.
Traditional single-frequency IMDD communication; OFDR-ISAC with and without sliding normalization; standalone sensing without communication; experimental and simulated conditions kept separate.
Original LFM probe versus pre-distorted probe; communication subcarriers SC1 and SC2; STPR swept while communication launch is fixed at 0 dBm.
Communication EVM before versus after sensing-assisted multipath compensation; electrical spectrum before versus after compensation.
HG0 and HG1 are compared for BER and phase-discriminator sensitivity; no external communication or sensing baseline is tested.
WinkLink is the primary reflected-OCC baseline; clean background images serve as the scene-recognition reference. Ablations remove or replace GANOCCAS components.
Communication is compared across temperature, vibration and connector offset. Sensing is compared before/after 1D-DnCNN and with/without vibration. IEEE 802.3cz is used as a setup context baseline.
Conventional processing without FPTs uses Max-FFT dynamic FOE, BPS and CMMA; FPT and no-FPT schemes are compared in simulation and on the same experimental data.
2ASK BER and eye diagrams are compared for fixed 280, 290 and 300 GHz carriers and the varying SFCW carrier. Device output power is characterized over 270-310 GHz.

RT-SS-guided dynamic spectrum access is compared with traditional static spectrum access for radar SINR/ranging and simulated imaging. Table 1 compares state-of-the-art electronic and photonic RT-SS systems.

Table 1 compares prior THz ISAC systems by data rate, modulation, ranging accuracy, sweep duration, sweep bandwidth and stated cost. The present work reports a lower 2 Gbit/s rate than cited offline high-order-QAM systems but online operation, no external modulator, approximately 1 cm ranging accuracy and a low-cost classification.

A mirror-mounted accelerometer is used as the vibration reference. Healthy and simulated-damage tower acceleration data from an external open benchmark are compared. Communication NGMI is compared with an assumed FEC threshold of 0.8167.
Wide-field illumination without structured illumination or without adaptive beamforming, depending on the experiment; all comparators remain condition-specific.

Communication behavior is compared among the optical ARoF setup, direct B2B SDR setup and simulation, but optical/B2B received powers differ and the authors treat the comparison as qualitative. Sensing estimates are compared with an accelerometer on the moving platform.

A conventional 1:8 or regular remote-node PON with parallel-path effect is compared with the serialized-trace passive remote node. RSSI is discussed as a coarse protocol-dependent alternative. Temperature sensing uses real versus masked return-loss readout, and UDP traffic is compared with regular/new remote nodes and with/without OTDR.
Traditional detector, standalone Bi-LSTM, Transformer, CNN, DNN and LCT communication detectors; 2D-FFT range/velocity estimator; OFDM ambiguity function without the hybrid network.
PAM-4, 16-QAM UFMC and PDM 16-QAM are compared as supported services; traditional pulse-based phi-OTDR frequency-response constraints are contrasted with continuous RBS sensing.
Conventional 16-QAM OFDM is the communication-BER and ambiguity-function/PSLR comparator under the same reported simulation settings.

Measured structured fields are compared with numerical predictions; Table 1 descriptively compares spiral phase plates, electronic UCAs, laser-array-driven UCAs and reconfigurable intelligent surfaces. The RELAX reconstruction is compared with the unprocessed two-dimensional Fourier result.

The closed-form suboptimal exposure algorithm is compared with an exhaustive numerical global optimum over 100 frequency ratios. Experimental normalized gains are compared with the theoretical Sinc exposure-response curves.

Primary matched baseline is a conventional photonics-aided dual-laser system evaluated under laser-linewidth sweeps. Communication comparisons use BER, EVM and SNR; sensing comparisons use PSLR and range-Doppler images.

Within-study configurations compare single FSO, 2x2 MIMO, 2x2 MIMO with compensator, 4x4 MIMO and 4x4 MIMO with compensator. Log-Normal and Gamma-Gamma turbulence are compared. Table 4 gives descriptive prior-work data-rate/range comparisons.

Each sensing result is compared with the same receiver processing without carrier-phase-noise retrieval. Low-speed and high-speed communication contexts are separately reported. Table I provides literature context but is not a controlled experimental comparator.

The two chip geometries S-LED/L-PD and L-LED/S-PD are directly compared for sensitivity, rise/fall time, transmission rate, linearity and detection range. Tables 2-3 provide literature context rather than controlled experimental baselines.

The source reports spectral efficiency 1.4177 bit/s/Hz above a prior single-carrier ISAC waveform [5]; this is not a same-apparatus controlled baseline. DC offset and UTC-PD optical input power are swept for communication BER, but sensing performance is not swept concurrently.

Figure 5 compares DSM Q-factor with versus without the sensing CP across protection-interval bandwidths, and Figure 8 directly compares 10 Hz strain sensitivity with communication off versus on. Figure 2 simulates one versus multiple sensing-diversity channels. Table 1 is literature context, not a controlled baseline.

Communication BER curves compare unperturbed FMF with 100 Hz and 200 Hz vibration. Sensing time traces and spectra compare LP11a and LP11b responses at the two vibration frequencies; no conventional sensor baseline or detection-accuracy benchmark is provided.

Communication simulation compares IM-LFM against PSK-LFM, CE-OFDM-LFM and QAM-LFM under standardized 1 microsecond pulses, 1 MHz PRF, about 30 Mbps and 1.027 GHz average bandwidth. Radar compares single- and dual-chirp/detection channels, multiple bandwidths, bandwidth intervals and ideal/non-ideal polarization/phase-noise conditions.

Beamforming is compared with conventional phase-shifter and delay-line TTD concepts and quantitatively with prior photonic TTD architectures in Table 1. ISAC compares 0 and -30 degree in-beam operation with out-of-beam placements and sweeps radar bandwidth (1-5 GHz) and communication symbol rate (200-800 Mbaud).

The report compares RF- and IF-mode communication, multiple QAM formats and launch powers, pilot phase-allocation methods, several STPRs/pilot intervals, multiple pilot sweep bandwidths, and frequency- versus phase-demodulated DAS. Exact pointwise plot coordinates are not transcribed.

The main controlled comparison is sensing with versus without the superimposed communication signal. The paper also reports BER versus received optical power and distinguishes ACO-OFDM from DCO-OFDM conceptually, but it does not experimentally benchmark alternative ISAC transmitter architectures.

The report compares communication and sensing across the same PSR sweep, measures receiver-power requirements separately, and compares SPT-based SISO-CMMA against conventional CMMA under identical emulated SOP rotations. Inner and outer subcarriers are also compared descriptively.

Residual BiLSTM is reported to outperform KNN, SVM and random forest on the same gesture/activity datasets. Device HR/SpO2 traces are visually compared with a commercial oximeter, but no numerical agreement error is reported. Indoor and outdoor classification conditions are reported separately.

A direct 265 nm LOS DCO-OFDM link provides the rate/misalignment benchmark. NLOS matched filtering is compared with photon counting. Smoke-free, dense-smoke and 90-minute dissipation states are compared using communication SNR and BER, but no calibrated reference aerosol concentration or dedicated smoke detector is used.

Communication is compared with plain QPSK and conventional DSSS at the same 5 Gbit/s. Phase uniformity compares DSSS-only, unperturbed ranging encryption and fully perturbed encryption. Ranging uses five measurements per step and simulation/theory comparators. Security sweeps 2, 4 and 6 cm decodable windows under a stated adversary model.

Measured five single-beam radiation patterns are compared with theoretical patterns; measured dual-beam patterns are compared with two-channel simulations, and a four-channel uniform-linear-array simulation evaluates potential crosstalk suppression. Actual TCR separations are compared with measured image separations.

Microcomb synchronization is compared with an external electronic clock having better oscillator phase-noise performance. Communication recovery is compared with and without FOE/CPE/full DSP. Measured 6.7 cm range resolution is compared with a source-calculated 6.6 cm nominal value; the 3.5 cm nominal azimuth resolution is analytical.

Within-study comparison of mono-static and bi-static sensing channels, each decomposed into total ISAC, target and background components. No measured V2V channel, non-ISAC communication baseline or alternative optical simulator is evaluated.

Sensing compares conventional versus frequency-filtered OFDM processing across linewidth/SNR and one/two targets. Communication compares FFT/subcarrier spacings and pilot-only versus PCPE-BPS recovery. Table 2 provides descriptive prior-system data-rate/resolution/resource comparisons.

The proposed FUA-UPE method is compared with the authors' earlier FOE-modified method under matched simulation parameters and with raw CPE phase in experiment. Table 3 qualitatively compares OFS-based, FOE-modified and FUA-UPE schemes by performance, cost and ease of integration; these qualitative labels are not converted to scores.

The dynamic optimal policy is compared within the same topology against a strongest-single-echo policy and a static all-active policy. Figure 2 compares network utilization and echo-signal gain across object positions; only percentages explicitly stated in text are extracted.

Within-device comparisons cover TENG grid widths, single/series/parallel coil configurations, sliding speeds, load resistance and capacitor sizes. No optical communication baseline, BER/data-rate comparator, clinical reference standard or external fall-detection comparator is reported.

TII-DGCNN accuracy is compared with PointNet and a traditional three-label meteorological-data method. Communication simulation compares the proposed nine-level modulation/power policy with a coarse BPSK/5 W versus 32QAM/5 W policy split at Cn2=5e-15.

Hamiltonian depth errors are compared with sinusoidal coding under the same 20 MHz setup. Single-frequency and multi-frequency operating points are compared in simulation and experiment, and communication-bit load is swept against depth error/BER.

Original RBS intensity is compared with subband-transformed/RVS synthesized intensity. Communication BER is swept against sensing incident power. No external communication baseline or alternative fading-suppression method is tested in the same experiment.

Proposed six-DoF SCA SLAP is compared with RSS-based six-DoF SLAP, TOA-based three-DoF VLP and RSS-based three-DoF VLP. Controls include perfect-CSI/no-interference variants, CRLBs, blocked/hostile LEDs and CPU time across LED/subcarrier counts.

Communication compares KK and conventional SSB reception, QPSK and 16-QAM, optical-comb and two-free-running-laser sources. Radar compares matched filtering alone with KK plus matched filtering, measured with theoretical range resolution, and one-/multipath simulations.

RFID coverage simulation compares four coordinated emitters with the same four emitters without phase coordination. Laboratory timing compares fixed bandwidth allocation with ordinary FTTR upstream access. No communication-rate/BER comparator is reported.

Communication NDR is swept versus AWG voltage and received optical power, then sensing-derived NDR estimates are compared with highest experimentally achievable NDR for three users. Radar resolution is compared with the theoretical 1.5 cm value; five target errors are compared with manual distance measurements.

Predictive steering is compared with otherwise matched steering without prediction across all three applications. Prediction error also uses no-prediction and per-application brute-force-optimal parameter baselines. Mobile BER is not directly observed but derived by authors from a separately characterized stationary APD/PD relationship.

Within-study sweeps compare 4 versus 8 subbands, QAM 16-256, roll-off 0-1, filter lengths 2/6/10/14, DC retained versus filtered and simultaneous versus individual AP transmission. Table I literature values are explicitly presented for information, not as comparable performance baselines.

Baseline 1 is LOS-only RSS SPAO with particle-swarm optimization; Baseline 2 is line-search RSS SPAO in diffuse scattering; Baseline 3 is gradient-descent SPAO using received OFDM signals. A TOA-plus-RSS CRLB is also plotted as a benchmark.

PLRC is compared experimentally with an OOK spread-spectrum scheme (SSS) under the same fiber-bench conditions at 10 and 50 Mbit/s; analytical comparisons also cover conventional phase-shift and RMCW ranging. DPSK and OOK BER requirements are compared under simulated weak turbulence.

Four controlled operating states isolate EOM and PZT contributions. Communication-only is compared with simultaneous communication plus vibration; sensing-only is compared with the simultaneous state. OTDR supplies position references.

The paper cites prior kbps DPIM and separate-waveform FMCW/OOK systems, and claims steering above 30 degrees relative to prior works, but provides no same-simulation conventional FMCW/QPSK or full-ring baseline table/curve.

With/without optical cancellation comparisons are repeated across SI spectra, EVM, ranging and imaging. PMI 1-12 is swept for communication BER versus radar SNR. No electronic-SIC or alternative photonic architecture is reproduced as an external baseline.

Measured sensing precision is compared with the shot-noise limit and with/without-vibration spectra identify affected nodes. SKR is calculated for three branches versus distance. No separate-QKD-only matched network, alternative sensing method or direct throughput baseline is tested.

LDBP training is compared with its initial uncompensated/initial-network SNR, and communication SNR is swept across LFM initial frequency, LFM bandwidth and launch power. SSFM-based DBP is discussed as a high-complexity reference but no numerical head-to-head complexity or performance result is reported.

Under the same simulated aperture, spectrum fusion is compared with single-BS distance-Doppler/ISAR and distributed-BS tomographic imaging. Field resolution is compared with the theoretical field configuration. Communication separately reports QPSK and 16-QAM BER/SNR; AROF pre-testing sweeps optical input power.

Communication compares ISAC-OF with conventional 56 Gbit/s PAM4 under B2B and 24.5 km conditions across received/launch powers and LFM bandwidth. Sensing compares PAM4-loaded ISAC-OF with a pure-LFM Phi-OTDR probe and varies enhancement factor, spatial resolution, launch power, LFM bandwidth and bit rate.

The sensing algorithm is compared with individual forward/backward Kalman-filter passes in simulation and with a fixed 5-50 kHz brickwall band-pass filter in experiment. The communication chain is described, but BER, GMI, received data rate or a communication baseline is not reported.

The EFPI uplink is colocated with a calibrated acoustic microphone: SNR, sensitivity and linearity are directly compared. Downlink sweeps headphone impedances (65/150/200 ohm) and custom single-/six-/eight-junction PPCs; no external communication-system baseline is tested.

Within-system four-condition comparison switches EOM/OOK and PZT/vibration on or off. Intensity versus phase demodulation, conventional sampling-rate resolution (16.4 m) versus phase-spectrum frequency-domain resolution (0.08 m), and prior literature distances/positioning are discussed; no external communication transceiver is experimentally benchmarked.

Estimated Monte Carlo BER is compared with theoretical BPSK BER; fiber lengths 10/25/50/75 km are compared within VPI; noiseless and two AWGN levels are compared for radar; one- versus two-target separations are tested. No external ISAC prototype is experimentally benchmarked.

Continuous event recording/software selection is compared conceptually with conventional range-gate hardware selection. Single-channel dead-time loss is modeled and a functioning SLR record is plotted. No joint optical-communication baseline or measured communication comparator is included.

The within-study comparator is unrestricted quantum detection/decoding versus conventional homodyne or heterodyne measurement. The conventional maximum intrusion-detection exponent is analytically one half of the optimal quantum value. No hardware or independent algorithm baseline is tested.

Within-study comparisons vary QPSK baud rate, LFMCW bandwidth, carrier frequency, ECL offset and DC offset. The most explicit baseline removes QPSK for radar (pure LFMCW SIR 17.12 dB) or removes LFMCW for communication (EVM 10.53%). Table 1 prior studies are contextual and were not extracted as this study's results.

OR baselines include GoogLeNet in preliminary interference tests and a CORE-Lens network without the Markovian discriminator in the main evaluation. OCC baseline is vanilla decoding of raw received frames; an ad-hoc filtered OCC pipeline is used in the latency comparison. Time-division OR/OCC is compared with concurrent CORE-Lens scheduling.
VLS angle estimates are compared with the servomotor's internal Hall sensor in dark and corrected ambient-light conditions. No communication BER, rate, packet-success or latency baseline is reported.

DBR versus no-DBR reflectance is compared, transmitted and received waveforms are shown at 50 and 150 kbps, and energy-harvester electrical characteristics are measured. BER, packet success, SNR and a conventional separate-component system baseline are not reported.

Two synthetic target ranges are compared with estimated range/velocity, and sent/received data are displayed. No conventional RF baseline, photonic-versus-electronic comparison, BER curve, noise/channel stress test or experimental measurement is reported.

B2B and 25 km transport, split numbers 250 and 500, and 6-18 GHz LO tuning are compared. Table 1 qualitatively compares component counts/features with prior works. No separate conventional electrical JRC baseline is experimentally tested.

Driving 4-6-GHz LFM versus generated 16-24-GHz LFM; triangular versus single-chirp ambiguity; chirp-polarity versus BPSK BER; basic versus 50/100-Mb/s sliced de-chirp; 180 versus 90 degree phase; uncoded versus length-7 DSSS; non-intra-pulse 4.883 Mb/s versus coded configurations.

Three communication rates and optical-power levels; radar targets/rates and eight carrier settings; 0-8 and high-band spectrum sensing with single/two-tone and multiformat SUTs; six-rate Monte Carlo radar-SNR comparison; Table I compares prior multifunctional systems.

Traditional OFDM versus CE-LFM-OFDM waveforms; frequency-doubling versus fundamental-frequency communication; phase-index and bandwidth sweeps; frequency-quadrupling versus doubling simulation; Table 3 contextualizes other CCFD systems but their values are not treated as outcomes of this study.

Communication compares radar-masked OFDM after SIC with OFDM-only and with no SIC. Radar compares multiple LFM-to-OFDM power ratios and an OFDM-absent condition. No external security method or attack baseline is evaluated.

Within-study comparison is single I or Q channel versus fused IQ channels and 2-GHz versus analytically discussed 4-GHz bandwidth. Prior-work values in the introduction are contextual only and are not extracted as this study's results.

Within-study comparisons vary chirp format, bandwidth-generation parameter k or T, input SNR and target delay/separation. No hardware baseline or alternative JRC receiver is experimentally compared; prior-work values in the introduction are contextual only.
Fixed versus adaptive GI, four constellations, several correlation-window lengths/distances and clipping ratios 1-13 dB are compared. Downlink and uplink BER are compared on matched hardware.
No quantitative baseline is simulated. Decoded waveform is compared with the expected differential sequence, and sensing peaks are shown for 10/20/30 m.
Single-user versus two-user performance, MLE versus quadratic fitting, and a conventional single Gaussian sensing pulse are compared. A raised-cosine pulse comparison is deferred to future work.

Communication BER is compared across four modulation orders; ranging is compared across correlation-symbol counts; positioning is compared for two transmitter-height geometries. No external ISAC baseline or experimental reference is evaluated.

Empirical Monte Carlo results are compared with known-theta theoretical BER; complexity is contrasted with an exponential brute-force joint search. No classical ISAC or hardware quantum baseline is evaluated.

The optimized capacity-distortion regions are compared across MAP, MLE and BCRB sensing costs, a high-O-SNR closed-form method, a Blahut-Arimoto-type method, communication-capacity upper/lower bounds, and communication- and sensing-optimal endpoints. No experimental LiDAR/FSO or external learned baseline is evaluated.

LFM-CPM is compared with CPM, which is the mu=0 communication-centric special case, and with theoretical BER lower bounds and asymptotic sensing CRB. The paper reports that LFM spreading can outperform CPM jointly in selected cases, while CPM remains an upper bound on rate for fixed modulation order.

The dynamic-motion control experiments compare directly communicated leader velocity through OISAC with a camera-sensing-only extended Kalman filter that estimates leader velocity. Packet-loss and display-delay tests characterize the optical link without a separate communication technology baseline.

Pure OFDM (beta=0), pure MLS (beta=infinity) and an OFDM-embedded PAM benchmark are compared with hybrid OFDM-MLS settings beta=1,2,3,5 and 10; BPSK/4QAM and MLS degrees 4/8 provide additional within-study comparisons.

Theoretical lower/upper BER bounds are compared with Monte Carlo results; MLE and MLE-plus-quadratic-fitting sensing are compared with CRB and a conventional single-pulse radar; user counts 1/2/4 and PN lengths 15-255 are varied.

Adaptive OIRS alignment is compared with a traditional FSO link without adaptive alignment. Analytical/asymptotic BER and outage are compared with Monte Carlo simulations across OIRS deflection, Sw/S, OIRS jitter, turbulence and speed values.
No-ADT UAVs are compared with ADTs containing 4, 7 and 10 total LED transmitters; Tx SNR and the heights of UAVs 2/3 are swept.

RBPSK-FMCW is compared with BPSK-FMCW and pure FMCW, two target reflectances, multiple phase differences/blank ratios/steering angles/data rates, an OPA-FMCW Lidar without OWC, and prior ISAC Lidar systems in Table I.

Two assumed optical-sensing SNR thresholds (10 and -10 dB), varied visibility, and trajectories with optimized beamwidth/bandwidth are compared. No no-sensing baseline, physical sensing estimator or experimental network is evaluated.

OFDM-MLS-CIM at alpha 0.1/0.3 is compared with pure OFDM at equal overall 132.8 Mbps, two bit-allocation modes, sensing with/without interference cancellation and varied cross-correlation windows/user distances.
Multiple HSM ratios and distances are compared; uplink 4-PAM versus 4-QAM OFDM and optical filtering versus no filtering are tested over 150-300 mV uplink amplitude.

Communication BER and ranging RMSE are compared with versus without wavelength filters; near and far users are compared across distance. No alternative sensing waveform or separate communication/sensing architecture is tested.

SUDO is compared against CUDO, which uses a UAV fixed horizontally at the cell center, and GBSO, which has no UAV. Two assumed sensing-SNR thresholds, 10 and -10 dB, represent channel-sensing quality.

PAPR is compared with the architecture in reference [10], which superimposes user OFDM signals before clipping. BER, sum rate and ranging RMSE/CRB are compared across author-specified power-allocation coefficients; there is no hardware baseline.

Optimized LACO-OFDM is compared against equal-power LACO-OFDM, optimized/equal-power ACO-OFDM and DCO-OFDM under shared optical/electrical power constraints; DCO bias is fixed at Pmax/2. Communication capacity is also compared with versus without SIC.
PMI is swept for BER and radar SNR; native two-2-GHz LFM resolution is contrasted with CFP 10-GHz-equivalent resolution. Five actual coordinates are compared with estimated positions.
ADO-OFDM is compared with ACO-OFDM and DCO-OFDM; original time-varying shot-noise and equivalent-AWGN models are compared; co-located and separated communication/sensing directions are compared.

Communication is shown by transmitted/received waveforms and a 40-Mbps eye diagram without a comparator. Sensing compares receiver photocurrent under air versus ethanol across a 2-10-mA current sweep; no competing sensor, communication-only matched device or simultaneous-operation baseline is tested.

Separate Fi-Wi and FSO communication tests are compared by EVM/path loss; standalone LFMCW and joint FDM configurations are both reported. The best separate values (24 Gbps and 0.03-m/384-m sensing) are not a simultaneous pair; the joint condition is 8 Gbps and 0.75-m/150-m sensing. No matched resource sweep or discrete-component baseline is tested.
Chromatic-dispersion compensation alone and DNN-DBP step sizes 80/40/20 km are compared; normal, single-loss, separated double-loss and same-span double-loss cases are evaluated.
Single versus paired Risley prisms, multiple exit angles/powers, and autocorrelation with versus without a prism are compared.
Matched filter, nonlinear matched filter and composite filter are compared; RCF versus no RCF and KK versus no KK are evaluated in simulation and experiment over carrier-to-signal power ratio.

SOP preprocessing time is compared directly with STFT, wavelet and Stockwell transforms for 300 data groups. Recognition is claimed superior to one similar-event study and more time-efficient than a segmented-STFT study, but matched datasets, full baseline implementations and statistical tests are not reported.

Method C (LFMW-based phase modulation) is compared with method A (standalone intensity modulation/conventional A-RoF) and method B (sinusoidal phase modulation) for SBS threshold; methods A and C are compared at matched injected powers for communication EVM, ACLR and channel power. Fiber-only and 3-m wireless results are also compared across bandwidth.

Communication bandwidth/rates of 4.5/18, 4/16 and 2/8 GHz/Gbps are compared. Radar compares single 1-GHz sub-bands, original CFP and PSO-improved CFP; sparse-FDM equivalent bandwidth is compared with conventional FDM and spectrum-sharing joint waveforms. Power ratio A2/A1 is swept against BER and de-chirped SNR.

Uniform 16-QAM is the main baseline; BI-PS 16-QAM at c0=1.20/1.12/1.02 and BWDM-PS are compared in simulation, with an additional PS-64-QAM extension. The laboratory experiment compares uniform and three BI-PS 16-QAM operating points at 6-dBm PD input through GMI/rate, SER, range profiles and main-to-sidelobe differences.

The unmodulated LFM waveform (0 Gbit/s) is the reference for normalized PSLR and range-estimation MSE; rates 2/4/6 Gbit/s are swept in theory, simulation and experiment. LFM-ASK is experimentally compared with LFM-PSK, showing about 3-dB PSLR loss, roughly 11-dB PSLR and about two-orders-worse BER despite remaining below SD-FEC.
Dual-band PFH is compared with traditional single-band TFH under broadband-noise jamming; single reference/agile bands and full-band/CFP are compared for ranging and ISAR imaging.
Electrical B2B, 800 m optical B2B, 40 km SMF and 40 km SMF plus DCM are compared with/without Gray coding; range statistics are reported for three optical configurations.
Sensing MSE and target-profile RMSE are compared with versus without interference cancellation at multiple QoS thresholds; communication BER is compared across thresholds from 0.10Pt to 0.50Pt.

Internal comparisons include polarization beam combiner versus ordinary optical coupler, 2.875 versus 5.75 GBd, single- versus dual-target ranging, received optical power, QAM-to-LFM power ratio, LO power/CSPR and laser-frequency offset. Literature baselines are contextual only.

Internal comparators include four waveform bandwidth cases, three SCM:LFM power ratios, carrier-frequency and Vpp sweeps, ROP variation, MZM QBP/MITP/MATP, PD versus BPD and HPF before/after conditions. Earlier Dong architectures are used as false-target-prone comparators in the imaging experiment but remain separate Phase-B studies.

Internal comparisons include BtB/10-km/20-km SMF, carrier-frequency and Vpp sweeps, LFM bandwidth, ROP, TFLN-MZM QBP/MITP/MATP and PD versus BPD. Table I literature rates/resolutions are contextual and are not treated as harmonized head-to-head experiments.

Communication is compared with standard QPSK and with/without LMS pilot removal; synchronization overhead is contrasted with a referenced conventional scheme; sensing autocorrelation is compared with a traditional unmodulated dual-chirp and Table I contextualizes prior photonic ISAC demonstrations.

The work motivates EO tuning against bulky GHz-band AWG generation and kHz-rate thermo-optic lasers, and plots BER across 1/3/5/8/10-Gbit/s OOK. It does not experimentally compare against a non-hopping ISAC baseline, inject jamming/inter-user interference or quantify a communication-sensing resource tradeoff.
CC-MUSIC is compared with conventional MUSIC for compute and single/multi-target accuracy, and with FFT ranging for PSLR/error/resolution; BER/EVM are measured versus received optical power.
Radar results are compared across 1/2 Gbit/s communication rates and 9-15/21-27 GHz ASK-LFM bands; measured ASK-LFM ranging resolution is compared with the unmodulated-LFM theoretical limit.
Communication BER/sensitivity is compared across OFDM, OTFS and DFT-OTFS; sensing error, PSLR and main-lobe width are compared with MSDMF, 2D-DFT, conventional MUSIC, TPE and zero-padding 2D-DFT.

Internal comparisons vary target/wireless distance, received optical power and LFM-QPSK overlap bandwidth. Table I literature comparisons are contextual and not harmonized experiments. The paper also contrasts photonic versus electrical dechirping/demodulation conceptually.

The proposed local MM solution is compared with a global optimum obtained using Mosek/CVX and with a fixed-AP benchmark having the same AP count in a room-center array. Reported curve values are not tabulated and were not digitized.

Communication equalization is compared against second-order truncated Volterra nonlinear equalization and feed-forward equalization. Sampling rates of 4 and 8 GSa/s are compared jointly. No external sensing baseline is tested.

FEA-TFW variants are compared against an earlier feature extractor, SVM/RF/KNN/NB classifiers, PCA/LDA/ICA reductions, previous two-layer RF co-cable results, and published SVM/2D-CNN vibration baselines. These are task-level sensing/classification comparisons, not communication baselines.

Uncalibrated versus end-channel-calibrated fits are compared for two representative events and seven-event validation. Table 4 qualitatively contrasts single-cable P/S time-difference and multi-cable-array positioning with the proposed single-wavefront method. There is no communication-performance baseline or measured sensing impact on live traffic.

ISAC and pure-communication BER/SNR curves are compared at equal incident optical power; sensing causes a slight BER deterioration while SNR is essentially unchanged, attributed to the guard band. Table I compares CRQ, distance, rate and resolution with prior systems, but no matched independent radar/communication hardware baseline is tested.

Simulations compare EVM with versus without CSS gain, giving >9-m versus 6-m 64-QAM coverage. Experiments sweep chirp bandwidth, data rate, photocurrent and three power ratios. Table II compares prior sensing receivers/tradeoff models. No independent nonphotonic hardware baseline is built.

P1 and P2 are compared against standalone THz-AP and a cited heterogeneous one-WiFi/four-VLC benchmark, with and without blockages, for average SE and outage. No physical system, measured channel or matched energy/hardware-cost comparison is provided.
Sensing cross-correlations with versus without homologous LO are compared; Table 1 benchmarks rate, resolution and CRQ against prior photonic JRC links.
OTFS communication is compared with OFDM; ZP-2D-DFT ranging is compared with traditional 2D-DFT using error, theoretical resolution, PSLR, main-lobe width and runtime.
PS-64QAM at k=3/5/7 is compared with uniform 64QAM; BWDM is compared with equal-rate CCDM for NGMI, sidelobe and operation count.

Manual hemocytometer-style cell counting is the density reference. Direct green-light optical-power measurement is an instrumental baseline and reaches only 0.35 maximum reported accuracy. QD colors and data rates are internally compared; orange gives 0.98 peak and 0.79 average accuracy for I. galbana.

DCO-OFDM and ACO-OFDM are simulated at the same effective data transmission rate. CEO-OFDM is reported to provide the best BER and smallest TDOA/distance/velocity errors, while using wider bandwidth. Analytical CRLB is compared with CEO-OFDM simulation MSE at N=256 and N=512.

An internal no-beamsteering configuration at M=16 is compared with the proposed three-orientation method: reported coverage is 6.30 m2 at 45 degrees and 0.11 m2 at 5 degrees without beamsteering, while beamsteering is said to improve coverage by 2.5-125 times. Two earlier multi-source experimental systems are cited contextually, but the authors explicitly do not claim a direct comparative evaluation.

Red, green and blue LDs are internally compared. Table IV reports optical input, harvested power and efficiency at mu=0. Published SLIPT systems are summarized contextually, but no matched external baseline is experimentally rerun. The related Phase-B candidate was human-adjudicated as a distinct study and is not pooled here.

Adaptive trajectory energy is compared with a non-adaptive fixed-normal-power VLC system. Baseline/unoptimized SNR and illuminance maps are compared with uniformity/enhanced optimization. There is no communication data-rate/BER baseline, physical localization baseline or independent sensing system.

Positioning is compared across identical uncorrected conversion ratios, constrained and unconstrained per-AP ratio calibration, and a second systematic error-vector correction. Communication sub-bands and AP positions are compared against the 3.8e-3 pre-FEC threshold. No separate sensing system, non-ISAC communication waveform or quantitative communication-rate-versus-positioning allocation sweep is evaluated.

SPPM-JSSPA and lower-complexity FSSPA are compared with slot-selection/uniform-power allocation (SSUPA) and random-slot-selection/uniform-power allocation (RSSUPA). Proposed methods consistently use less sensing, communication and total power; FSSPA is close to SPPM-JSSPA with lower complexity.

Hybrid MLS-OFDM is compared with conventional pure OFDM across DC and Vpp. Pure OFDM has better BER, hybrid MLS-OFDM has substantially better ranging RMSE, and AC waveform choice has little influence on harvesting. Within the hybrid waveform, p1 and p2 sweeps expose continuous tri-functional tradeoffs.
No separate baseline architecture is quantitatively evaluated; parameter sweeps compare chirp bandwidth/duration and 200 Mbps, 1 Gbps and 5 Gbps communication rates.
VehicleTalk with Raptor Codes is compared against a circular-shift non-encoding scheme for goodput at k=50 and k=100; communication and sensing are also evaluated versus distance.
KNN is the HGR baseline; one- versus two-carrier motivation, in- versus cross-scene training, bReflexGest versus KNN, and cReflexGest versus KNN are evaluated.
Direct oscilloscope OFDM constellations are compared with ISMD-down-converted constellations for QAM4-QAM64; fiber versus no-fiber frequency response and simulated compensation are compared.
Communication BER is compared across carrier frequency and two link distances; localization is compared before and after beam-splitter calibration against ground-truth distance.

Uncoded overlap, strict resource separation and partial separation are conceptual baselines; event results compare ideal standalone DAS, non-ideal DAS and protected IOSAC/OCDMA. Code assignment compares random versus minimax subsets.

SVM, decision tree and random forest are compared on the same seven-class dataset using accuracy, precision, recall and F1. No camera/wearable/WiFi/radar sensing baseline and no communication-only or concurrent-payload VLC baseline is experimentally tested.

Optical sensing-flow aggregation is compared with transport without optical switching as target count grows. RU4-only and RU5-only target heatmaps are compared, and sensing traffic is evaluated across velocity-resolution settings. Numerical bar coordinates are not tabulated and were not digitized.

SIC and no-SIC are compared for adjacent and separated tag regions at OSR 10/20; several retroreflectors, four LC shutters and two receiver architectures are experimentally compared. Single-region ranging is stratified by center/mid/edge. No full multi-tag physical baseline is reported.

The proposed joint method is compared with particle swarm optimization, fixed processing-frequency, fixed power, fixed 0.5 offloading and full-offloading algorithms. Reported curves show the proposed method converges quickly and has the lowest overall latency, while full offloading is worst in the nominal comparison. No physical VLC/VLS baseline or sensing-accuracy comparator is provided.

VBKF-CPPRS is compared with KF and VBKF-MA for tracking RMSE/time and with exhaustive beam traversal for search time. HWPSO-SD is compared with average-value, fixed-weight, soft-judgment, KF and CNN phase estimators for mean/variance of BER and computation time. Physical ranging is compared with theoretical resolution and known target locations; no separate radar-plus-radio hardware baseline or end-to-end train trial is reported.
Broad-linewidth 21.4 MHz DFB transceivers are compared with 200 kHz lasers for phase noise, NGMI and vibration recovery; prior low-cost transmission and forward-sensing studies are benchmarked.
12.5 MHz DFB transmitter is compared with a 100 kHz ECL for phase noise, NGMI and vibration spectra; BTB and 480 km conditions are compared.

Sensing recognition is compared among joint SOP-plus-phase, SOP-only and phase-only CNN inputs in a representative trial and five independent shuffles. Communication BER is compared with and without the sensing tap. SOP and phase sensing SNR/robustness are also compared.

Table I compares prior photonic multifunction systems on communication frequency/data rate, radar frequency/error or resolution and spectrum range/error. Within the proposed testbed, X-polarization power splits are compared for generated-signal amplitude/SNR and spectrum-sensing pulse detectability.

Conventional pulse DAS is compared with equal-energy LFM pulse-compression DAS, and co-propagation is compared with counter-propagation in simulations and experiments. Single-polarization simulation isolates polarization-rotation effects from XPM phase noise.
Channel estimation is compared with LS, OMP, gOMP and DNN; positioning with KNN, SVR, RF and DNN; online MTFL is compared with centralized MTL under environmental switches.
Turbulence-adaptive Fresnel-shaped beams are compared with a conventional Gaussian beam under two reversed strong/weak turbulence distributions at five communication rates.

Single-, double- and triple-component DAS in SSMF and triple-component SDM-DAS in seven-core fiber are compared for sensitivity, fading and bandwidth. Conventional DAS is compared with SDM-DAS at 200, 2100, 3100 and 6100 Hz. Communication is tested across all cores/wavelengths, sensing-off/on, cores with/without sensing and three sensing-EDFA drive levels. Prior ISAC capacities/sensitivities are tabulated.

NCS sub-sampling-point delay estimation is compared with conventional symbol/sampling-point correlation and with the G.984 +/-3-ns ranging specification. Optical back-to-back, 50G 20-km and 200G 20-km cases; 0.25-ps versus 1-ps nominal settings; bandwidth and SNR sweeps are separated.

Sensing with and without CDM modulation, launch-power and CSPR sweeps, LFM versus single-frequency carrier BER, QPSK versus 16-QAM, uncompensated versus pre-compensated/PCS 16-QAM, B2B versus 10-km fiber versus fiber-wireless, and direct 28-GHz versus 3-GHz optical upconversion are compared.

First- versus seventh-order harmonic, with versus without analog frequency multiplier, multiple DFT lengths, 20 versus 60 degrees C, and launched optical power are compared. Communication interference is assessed by Q factor and constellation across temperature/power.

Nine simulated TDM allocations quantify communication data rate versus radar detection range. Experimental BER compares 10-GBaud 16QAM and 64QAM versus PD input power. Measured target displacement/resolution is compared with physical spacing and a 1.5-cm theoretical bandwidth limit.

Non-reciprocity error curves are compared across vibration positions, noise-free versus 25 dB OSNR, 100-Hz phase noise versus phase-noise-free conditions, frequencies and amplitudes. The architecture is qualitatively contrasted with bidirectional/synchronized and dual-wavelength/ultra-wideband localization schemes.

NRZ and PAM4 random envelopes are compared for correlation, largest Lyapunov exponent and permutation entropy; injection power/detuning, LFM:PAM4 power ratio, phase-modulation depth, received power, transmission distance and wavelength/dispersion/delay mismatch are evaluated as operating-point comparisons.

With versus without spectrum spreading is compared for BER/SNR, four coding rates are compared for PSR and autocorrelation width, spread gains are compared for required SNR, and prior photonic/electronic JRC systems are tabulated for rate and range resolution.
4-, 16- and 64-QAM at 4 versus 6 GBaud are compared by BER/ROP; single-target measured versus actual range and dual-target measured versus actual separation are compared.

BPSK and QPSK EVM/BER are compared across baud rates and received power; measured target spacings are compared with 6-, 10- and 100-cm ground truth; prior JRC systems are tabulated by rate, spectrum efficiency, radar bandwidth and LO need.

Autocorrelation is contrasted with cross-correlation between chaotic signals generated at different times; communication recovery is shown across distance, and radar estimates are compared with actual target distance.
Sensing-only is compared with integrated OTN+sensing; counter-propagating operation is compared with co-propagating operation at 2.582- and 0.632-THz wavelength spacings.

Integrated ITVFS-SCSM is compared with typical OFDM for BER; communication-induced sensing crosstalk is modeled; sensing SNR is swept over launch power; localization results are compared with true positions.
No common benchmark baseline is evaluated. Anti-jamming comparison contrasts fixed-initial-frequency and frequency-agile LFM sets under stated blocking interference.

Internal comparisons cover two QAM allocations, baud rates, 130 versus 150 GHz, pure LFMCW versus two SCIE formats for ranging, and single- versus multiple-LFMCW generation. Literature values in comparison tables are contextual and were not extracted as this study's outcomes.

Qualitative comparison with conventional ocean-bottom seismometers and fixed-point sensors; official Guangdong Seismological Bureau records corroborate selected microseisms. No communication baseline, throughput/BER measurement or controlled sensing baseline is reported.
Within-study frequency-division and joint-waveform architectures; the 2025 conference configuration is supplementary and condition-specific. External Table 1 comparators are not P03 outcomes.

The journal compares TDM, FDM and CTCF photonic JRC literature in Table I, and experimentally compares 11.5- versus 23-GHz/GBaud modes, carrier/IF sweeps and polarization-crosstalk conditions. SCR-00886 is the eligible preliminary conference companion.

Within-report comparisons cover ten TFDM cases in the journal/conference, six FDM bandwidth ratios in the 2022 companion, full-band communication/radar endpoints, FDM/TDM/hybrid forms, back-to-back versus 10-km fiber, and parameter sweeps for Vpp/ROP. Cross-report numbers are not treated as matched baselines because modulation and resource grids differ.
